key_insight: REFLEX uses a fast typed decision layer (Jev) to defer only low-confidence or generative cases to a strong LLM, cutting expensive calls while keeping task success high.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical control strategy for LLM agents: replace many routine decisions with cheaper selective routing, and reserve strong-model inference for boundary cases and hard actions.
method: Use Jev as a typed, low-latency decision layer for bounded actions.
Fallback to a strong LLM only when confidence is low or free-form generation is needed.
Test selective control against multiple fallback families and boundary-condition interventions.
evidence_signal: On a frozen 100-task benchmark, REFLEX reached 95% success while reducing strong-model calls by 72.7%; external BFCL and τ-style evaluations showed only limited gains over a cheap generative cascade when routing was already highly accurate.
watch_item: Benefits appear smaller when ordinary routing is already very accurate, so implementation gains may depend strongly on action-set size and the presence of near-valid alternatives near authorization boundaries.
paper_title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
